title: Generation 2 Stage 3 gate criteria — Gate 3 development admissibility, evaluation methods fixed before results
declaration_note: Generation 2 inherits Generation 1's Gate 3 criteria unchanged wherever they are measurable as written. Two are not: S3-C5's reconstruction assumes non-overlapping trades, which a portfolio holding up to three positions violates, and S3-C7's neighbour set is hard-coded to exactly four, which a three-axis grid does not produce. Both are redefined here, before any Generation 2 result exists, with the divergence from the Generation 1 method stated rather than absorbed. Everything else — thresholds, predicates, undefined-case handling, and the treatment of NOT_EVALUABLE — is carried over verbatim, so a reader comparing the two files sees exactly two differences and can check that they are the two declared here.

relationship_to_generation_1_criteria.seal_check: The Generation 2 evaluator calls the existing stockedge100.strategies.gate.check_thresholds_against_seal against this file, so the five frozen thresholds, the S3-C6 predicate text, and the S3-C4 exception flag are asserted to be unchanged from the constitution before any condition is evaluated.

frozen_gate_text_verbatim: This gate rejects obviously weak or fitted candidates before sealed evaluation. Pass only if, on development data after base costs: total return is positive; maximum drawdown is no worse than 15%; profit factor is at least 1.10; at least 30 closed trades exist, unless a lower-frequency protocol predeclared a longer evidence requirement before results; performance is not dependent on one trade: removing the single best trade leaves total return above 0%; no single instrument contributes more than 50% of total strategy profit for a multi-instrument strategy; reasonable neighboring parameter values do not reverse the sign of net return. Fail verdict: STRATEGY_REJECTED_IN_DEVELOPMENT.

conflicts_found.description: The frozen JSON companion for gate 3 carries five thresholds. The frozen Markdown carries seven conditions: the same five plus the profit-concentration condition and the neighbouring-parameter sign-stability condition.
conflicts_found.resolution: The Markdown is authoritative and more restrictive. All seven conditions are evaluated and all seven must pass.
conflicts_found.action_taken: Reported, not repaired. No frozen artifact is edited.

conflicts_found.status: inherited from Generation 1, unchanged, and materially more load-bearing in Generation 2
conflicts_found.description: Gate 3 requires maximum drawdown no worse than 15%. Constitution section 5.1 puts the research shutdown at exactly 15% below the running high-water mark. The two thresholds are the same number.
conflicts_found.resolution: Any variant that trips the shutdown has by construction breached S3-C2, and its equity curve is flat from liquidation onward because entries are permanently blocked.
conflicts_found.generation_2_note: In Generation 2 this is not merely a structural remark. The frozen representative-selection rule screens on zero shutdown events, so the selected representative has by construction never breached 15% intra-run — which means S3-C2 is very likely to be MET for whichever variant the rule selects. That is a consequence of the selection rule, not evidence about the hypothesis, and it is stated here so that a MET verdict on S3-C2 is not read as an independent confirmation.

conflicts_found.description: S3-C5's Generation 1 measurement reconstructs equity sequentially as E[i] = E[i-1] + pnl[i] over closed trades in exit order, and states explicitly that this is exact 'because the sealed cost model permits at most one open risky position, trades are sequential and non-overlapping'. Generation 2 holds up to three positions at once, so trades overlap and the sequential reconstruction is no longer exact: it would charge a trade's P&L against an equity base that already contains P&L from a trade running concurrently with it.
conflicts_found.resolution: The per-trade multiple is redefined against the equity base that actually existed when the trade was entered: r[i] = 1 + pnl[i] / E_entry[i], where E_entry[i] is account equity at the close of the session immediately preceding that trade's entry fill, or starting equity if there is no such session. Both removals required by the Generation 1 method are kept, both must still leave a positive value, and the equity-curve total return is reported alongside with the difference disclosed rather than reconciled away. See condition S3-C5 below for the full procedure.
conflicts_found.action_taken: Declared before any Generation 2 result exists. The Generation 1 method is not edited and its file is not touched; Generation 2 uses its own module.

conflicts_found.description: S3-C7's Generation 1 implementation, stockedge100.strategies.gate.condition_7, raises ConfigViolation unless exactly four robustness neighbours are supplied, because Generation 1's protocol declared exactly four per candidate. Generation 2's neighbours are derived from a three-axis grid and number between three and five depending on where in the grid the representative lands.
conflicts_found.resolution: Generation 2 defines its neighbour set structurally — every variant differing from the representative in exactly one axis by exactly one step, on the orderings lookback 3 < 6 < 12, k 1 < 2 < 3, frequency MONTHLY < QUARTERLY — and evaluates the same sign-stability predicate over that set in its own module. The rule is a function of the representative's grid position and is fixed here, so the neighbour set cannot be chosen after the representative is known.
conflicts_found.consequence: Neighbour count is 3 when the representative is at a corner of all three axes, 5 when it is interior on both the lookback and k axes, 4 otherwise. All neighbours are already members of the eighteen-variant grid and are already run, so no additional run is created by this condition and no new parameterisation is introduced.
conflicts_found.action_taken: Declared before any Generation 2 result exists. Generation 1's condition_7 is not modified.

conflicts_found.description: The Generation 2 operating instruction names the verdict tokens STAGE_3_G2_STRATEGY_ADMITTED_IN_DEVELOPMENT and STAGE_3_G2_NO_CANDIDATE. Neither string exists in any Generation 1 artifact, and the project rule is that a verdict token comes from disk rather than from a prompt. Separately, the fail token is not the negation of the constitution's frozen fail_result for gate 3, which is STRATEGY_REJECTED_IN_DEVELOPMENT; it names the absence of a candidate rather than the rejection of one.
conflicts_found.resolution: This file is the disk. Both tokens are sealed here, before any Generation 2 strategy module exists and before any variant is run, so neither can be shaped by an outcome. The constitutional fail_result is recorded alongside as the equivalent under the constitution's own naming, and the Generation 2 report states both. The instruction's token is the one emitted, because the instruction is the authorizing instrument for this generation and the constitution's own token is not weakened by the rename — a failure is still a failure and no candidate advances either way.
conflicts_found.action_taken: Sealed here before results. No sealed Generation 1 derivation is edited to match.

conflicts_found.description: Generation 1 evaluated Gate 3 as a disjunction across six independently declared candidates. Generation 2 declares one candidate whose parameterisation is fixed by a frozen return-blind selection rule over eighteen variants.
conflicts_found.resolution: The gate is evaluated on the single selected representative. The disjunction of constitution section 9 is over a candidate set of size one. Evaluating all eighteen and passing the stage if any one of them passes would be the multiplicity abuse the selection rule exists to prevent, and would make the selection rule decorative.
conflicts_found.action_taken: Declared before any result. The other seventeen variants are reported descriptively and are never used to reach a verdict.

verdict_token_derivation.pass_condition: The representative selected by the frozen return-blind rule in SE100-CFG-3101 satisfies EVERY hard condition of Gate 3 on its base-cost development run.
verdict_token_derivation.fail_condition: Either no representative exists, because every one of the eighteen variants recorded at least one research-shutdown event, or a representative exists and does not satisfy every hard condition.
verdict_token_derivation.conjunctive_note: Constitution section 9: gates are conjunctive; every hard condition must pass, and NOT_RUN, UNKNOWN, NOT_EVALUABLE, or missing evidence is not a pass. Conjunction applies WITHIN a candidate. Generation 2 declares one candidate, so the cross-candidate disjunction is over a set of size one — see G2-CONFLICT-15.
verdict_token_derivation.token_naming_note: See G2-CONFLICT-12. The instruction's fail token names the absence of an admissible candidate; the constitution's names the rejection of one. They denote the same stage outcome and both are recorded in the decision package.
verdict_token_derivation.other_tokens_available: BLOCKED_BY_DATA, BLOCKED_BY_INFRASTRUCTURE, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, INVALIDATED, NOT_RUN, per constitution section 10. Missing evidence may never be converted to PASS or NOT_APPLICABLE for convenience.
verdict_token_derivation.fail_is_a_deliverable: FAIL — STAGE_3_G2_NO_CANDIDATE is a legitimate and fully anticipated outcome. It is recorded, kept on disk, and does not license a nineteenth variant, a re-run with a different grid, or a promotion of the runner-up.
verdict_token_derivation.neither_token_is_a_stage_verdict_for_any: These two tokens belong to Generation 2 Stage 3 alone. No Generation 2 artifact at any other stage may emit either.

conditions.measurement: total_return over the representative's base run, from stockedge100.backtest.metrics.total_return on the engine equity curve: final equity / starting equity - 1, exact Decimal.
conditions.costs: base cost model, all costs already charged inside the equity curve
conditions.not_evaluable_treatment: An equity curve with fewer than two points is NOT_EVALUABLE and fails.

conditions.required_verbatim: maximum drawdown is no worse than 15%
conditions.measurement: max_drawdown from stockedge100.backtest.metrics: the largest peak-to-trough decline of the daily closing equity curve, expressed as a non-negative fraction of the running peak. Session-close granularity; the project holds no intraday data and none is imputed.
conditions.interaction: See S3-CONFLICT-3, including the Generation 2 note: the selection rule makes a MET verdict here close to structural, and it is not independent evidence.

conditions.measurement: profit_factor from stockedge100.backtest.metrics over CLOSED trades only: gross profit divided by gross loss, where a trade's P&L is exit cash plus dividends received while held minus entry cash, with both legs' costs already inside those cash figures. A trade is a round trip: one entry fill and the exit fill that closes it.

undefined_cases.no_closed_trades: profit_factor is null. Recorded as NOT_EVALUABLE and the condition FAILS. It is not passed by default and not marked not-applicable.
undefined_cases.no_losing_trades: profit_factor is null because gross loss is zero. If closed trades exist and gross profit is positive, this is recorded as UNDEFINED_NO_LOSSES_TREATED_AS_MET, with the raw null preserved in the evidence rather than replaced by a number. The sealed cost model requires profit factor undefined when there are no losses to be reported as null, never as infinity.

conditions.generation_2_note: With up to three concurrent positions a single rebalance can close several trades at once. That changes the trade count, not the definition: each round trip is still one trade and each contributes its own P&L to the gross profit or gross loss sum.

conditions.required_verbatim: at least 30 closed trades exist, unless a lower-frequency protocol predeclared a longer evidence requirement before results
conditions.measurement: Count of closed round-trip trades in the engine's trade log for the representative's base run. A position still open on the final session is not closed and is not counted; at k = 3 up to three positions may be open on the final session and none of them counts.
conditions.exception_note: No Generation 2 variant invokes the lower-frequency exception. The exception permits a LONGER evidence requirement, not a smaller trade count, so it could not lower this floor in any case. Recorded explicitly and before results so that a quarterly variant cannot be argued into it once its trade count is known. See SC-1 in SE100-CFG-3101 for the structural risk that a low-turnover quarterly k=1 variant falls short of 30.

conditions.required_verbatim: performance is not dependent on one trade: removing the single best trade leaves total return above 0%

measurement.why_the_generation_1_basis_does_not_tran: Generation 1 reconstructed equity as E[i] = E[i-1] + pnl[i] over closed trades in exit order, exact because at most one position could be open so trades never overlapped. Generation 2 holds up to three positions concurrently. Under the sequential reconstruction, two trades opened on the same rebalance would be charged against different equity bases purely because of the order they happened to close in, and the second would be credited with an equity base already inflated by the first. The reconstruction would not be wrong by a rounding error; it would be measuring a different thing.
measurement.basis: Closed trades only. Each trade's multiple is taken against the equity that actually existed when that trade was entered, which is well defined whether or not other positions were open at the time.
procedure: For the i-th closed trade, E_entry[i] = account equity at the CLOSE of the session immediately preceding that trade's entry fill, read from the engine's own equity curve. If the entry fill is on the first session of the run, E_entry[i] = starting equity = 100.00.
Per-trade equity multiple r[i] = 1 + pnl[i] / E_entry[i].
Reconstructed total return = product of all r[i], minus 1.
Best-trade-removed return = product of r[i] for i not equal to j, minus 1.
measurement.which_trade_is_removed: Two removals are computed and BOTH must leave a positive return. j1 is the trade with the largest equity multiple r[i]. j2 is the trade with the largest absolute P&L pnl[i]. These usually coincide and need not. Requiring both is the stricter reading, carried over unchanged from Generation 1, and it is fixed here so the stricter or looser reading cannot be chosen after seeing which one the representative survives.
measurement.tie_handling: If several trades tie on the maximum, the earliest by index is removed. Carried over from Generation 1's max(..., key=(value, -index)) tiebreak so that the removal is deterministic.
measurement.relation_to_headline_return: The reconstruction is NOT expected to equal the equity-curve total return, and no attempt is made to make it equal. Concurrent positions mean the products do not telescope; dividends credited outside a trade and positions still open on the final session also contribute. Both figures are reported side by side, together with their difference, and the condition is evaluated on the reconstruction, whose purpose is to be a like-for-like comparison against the same reconstruction with one trade removed.
measurement.disclosure_requirement: The Stage 3 (Generation 2) report states the reconstructed return, the equity-curve return, and the gap between them explicitly. A material gap is a limitation to disclose, not a defect to reconcile.

conditions.not_evaluable_treatment: Fewer than two closed trades is NOT_EVALUABLE and fails; a result that is one trade is the exact dependence this condition tests for.
conditions.implementation: stockedge100.strategies.g2_gate, which implements this basis. Generation 1's stockedge100.strategies.gate.condition_5 is not called for Generation 2 and is not modified.

conditions.required_verbatim: no single instrument contributes more than 50% of total strategy profit for a multi-instrument strategy
conditions.generation_2_status: unchanged from Generation 1 in measurement and predicate; the applicability question resolves differently and the reason is stated
conditions.measurement: For each instrument, contribution = sum of pnl over that instrument's closed trades, divided by the sum of pnl over all closed trades. Evaluated only when total closed-trade P&L is strictly positive; when total P&L is zero or negative the share is not a meaningful proportion and the case is recorded as NOT_EVALUABLE — which is moot, because S3-C1 has already failed such a candidate.

scope_interpretation.rationale: Applicability is decided by the DECLARED universe, never by the realized symbol count. A candidate that declares one instrument cannot have a concentration problem the condition could detect, so it is NOT_APPLICABLE_BY_CONDITION_TEXT. A candidate that declares many and then trades one is exactly the case this condition exists to catch, so it remains applicable and fails. Carried over verbatim in effect from Generation 1, and it is the key stockedge100.strategies.gate.condition_6 reads for its not-applicable note.
scope_interpretation.why_it_always_applies: Generation 2's declared universe is the full 34-member frozen list at every rebalance, so the strategy is multi-instrument by declaration regardless of how many symbols it turns out to trade. Deciding applicability from the realized count would let a candidate that collapsed onto one symbol escape the condition precisely when it is most informative.
scope_interpretation.single_instrument_treatment: Not reachable in Generation 2. Retained in the schema so this file remains comparable to SE100-CFG-3002.
scope_interpretation.generation_2_significance: This is the condition that tests the claim in the charter's section 2. Generation 1's validated candidate put 100% of its profit into SPY. If Generation 2's representative does the same, this condition fails and the stage fails, which is the correct outcome: a rotation strategy that never rotates has not demonstrated the thing Generation 2 exists to test.

conditions.required_verbatim: reasonable neighboring parameter values do not reverse the sign of net return

measurement.neighbour_definition: Every variant in the eighteen-variant grid that differs from the representative in exactly one axis by exactly one step.
measurement.one_step_note: A step is to an adjacent value in the ordering above. From lookback 3 the only neighbour is 6, not 12. From k = 2 both 1 and 3 are neighbours. The frequency axis has two values, so its single neighbour is always the other one.
measurement.neighbour_count: 3 when the representative is at an endpoint of both the lookback and the k axis; 5 when it is interior on both; 4 otherwise. The count is a function of the representative's grid position and is not chosen.
measurement.no_new_runs: Every neighbour is already a declared member of the grid and is already run under the same window and the same base cost model with the research shutdown enforced. This condition creates no new parameterisation and no new run.
measurement.what_is_read: Each neighbour's base-run total return and its sign. Nothing else about a neighbour enters this condition.

conditions.predicate: sign(neighbour total_return) == sign(representative total_return) for EVERY neighbour, where sign is positive, negative, or zero and zero matches nothing
conditions.selection_prohibition: Neighbour runs are read for the sign of net return and nothing else. No neighbour is ever promoted to representative, and the representative's parameterisation is never revised because a neighbour did better. Doing so would be a material change under constitution section 11 and would create a new candidate restarting at Gate 3. It would also destroy the return-blind property of the selection rule, since the promotion would be driven by a return.
conditions.not_evaluable_treatment: A neighbour that fails to run is NOT_RUN, which is not a pass; the condition fails.
conditions.implementation: stockedge100.strategies.g2_gate. Generation 1's condition_7 raises ConfigViolation on a neighbour count other than four and is not called for Generation 2; it is not modified.

reported_but_not_gating: The representative's stress run, in full. The stress cost assumption gates nothing at Gate 3, exactly as in Generation 1, and its figures are reported so a later gate reads them from evidence rather than re-deriving them.

All eighteen variants' return, maximum drawdown, profit factor, closed trade count, and shutdown event count, for both runs. Descriptive record only; see SE100-CFG-3101 reported_for_every_variant_but_not_gating.
CAGR, annualised volatility, Sharpe ratio at a 0.00% risk-free rate, exposure fraction, win rate, average win, average loss, longest flat streak, distinct symbols traded, and per-symbol contribution.

SPY total return and SPY tradable buy-and-hold over the representative's own window, with the research shutdown both enforced and disabled, the latter explicitly labelled a benchmark reference account; the cash benchmark at 0.00% annual; and the do-nothing benchmark.

Constitution section 4 requires better risk-adjusted performance than cash for a strategy to pass overall, and beating SPY is not mandatory where drawdown is materially reduced. Neither is among the seven hard conditions of Gate 3, so neither gates this stage.
evaluation_integrity_rules: Conditions are evaluated by a program that reads the engine's own outputs. No condition verdict is typed by hand into a report.
Every condition verdict is one of MET, NOT_MET, NOT_EVALUABLE, or NOT_APPLICABLE_BY_CONDITION_TEXT. There is no fifth value and no borderline value.
The candidate's admissibility is the conjunction of its applicable conditions. NOT_EVALUABLE never counts as MET.
Thresholds are compared as exact Decimals. No comparison is made in floating point, and no result is rounded before comparison.
The evidence file records the measured value alongside every verdict, so a reader can recompute the comparison without rerunning the engine.

The representative is selected before any condition is evaluated, by the return-blind rule in SE100-CFG-3101. Condition evaluation cannot feed back into selection, because selection has already happened and is not repeated.
If the representative fails any condition, the stage fails. No other variant is evaluated against the gate.

windows.enforcement: ResearchWindow raises WindowViolation on any session outside the development window, MarketView raises LookAheadError on any read past the decision session, and stockedge100.strategies.g2_window_guard adds the three Generation 2 checks sealed in STAGE_1_G2_PARTITION_LOCK.md section 4. All are structural; none depends on a strategy behaving well.
windows.disclosed_limitation_reference: Any Generation 2 report that references the validation window reproduces the disclosure text of STAGE_1_G2_PARTITION_LOCK.md section 2 verbatim. This stage does not read the validation window at all.
